question: Should OpenClaw expose `sessions_spawn.tools` as an immutable persisted per-child capability boundary, including deny rules and CLI fail-closed rejection, or should the feature be narrowed before core adoption?
rationale: This is not merely an implementation choice: it defines a public control-plane API and durable authority model for subagents, while the canonical request still carries explicit product and security-review signals.

options.title: Approve the persisted policy contract
options.body: Confirm that `"none"` and allow/deny semantics are the intended core API, then require final-head runtime proof and the normal release-owned changelog handling.

options.title: Narrow to an allow-only initial scope
options.body: Keep a simpler embedded-runtime restriction if maintainers do not want deny semantics or durable policy behavior in the first public version.

options.title: Defer to the canonical design issue
options.body: Pause this PR until the remaining policy and security questions are resolved in the linked canonical issue.

recommendation.title: Approve the persisted policy contract
recommendation.body: Confirm that `"none"` and allow/deny semantics are the intended core API, then require final-head runtime proof and the normal release-owned changelog handling.
